confirmed.reasoning: GTKX is at fault, and none of the rule-out grounds hold. (1) No GTK4/Adwaita/GLib API is involved: this is entirely CLI/config file management in @gtkx/cli. (2) The reproduction uses the option exactly as documented. website/guide/configuration-and-codegen.md:33 states "`codegen: false`: skips generation, so the project imports whatever binding store is already installed", and packages/cli/src/commands/codegen.ts:26 prints "codegen: disabled for this project; reusing an installed binding store". Nothing in the guide restricts the option to monorepo sub-packages or warns that it removes anything. (3) Not a duplicate. The nearest ledger entry, F101, is about the store being *written* to a node_modules the build cannot resolve under hoisting; resolve-store.ts in this worktree already carries the `nodeModules` anchor F101 asked for. No ledger entry covers store deletion under `codegen: false`. (4) Not a machine artifact: I reproduced it on a fresh copy of the template in my own scratchpad through a different command than the report used (`gtkx build`, i.e. the `ensureGenerated` call site at line 216, not the `gtkx codegen` call site at line 131). `node_modules/.gtkx` went from `env.d.ts gi jsx` to `env.d.ts` alone, both `node_modules/@gtkx/{gi,jsx}` links vanished, and the build then failed with `Cannot resolve "@gtkx/gi/gdk": … Add "Gdk-4.0" to libraries`. `npx gtkx codegen --force` afterwards printed the "reusing an installed binding store" line and left the store empty. The code path is an unconditional `rmSync(..., {recursive: true, force: true})`, so no environment can affect it. (5) Not a missing feature: the feature exists, is documented, and the implementation does the opposite of the documented contract. Reading the source makes the origin plain. `removeSharedStoreShadow` resolves four paths against the project root — `node_modules/.gtkx/gi`, `node_modules/.gtkx/jsx`, `node_modules/@gtkx/gi`, `node_modules/@gtkx/jsx` — and deletes them. Those are precisely the paths `resolveStore` in packages/codegen/src/store/resolve-store.ts (`storeOptions(runtime.nodeModules, "gi", …)` at line 99, with `resolvePackage` walking `nodeModulesChain` from the project root) chooses for a standalone project that installs `@gtkx/runtime` and `@gtkx/react` itself. The helper was introduced in 43547a62 for the in-repo examples (examples/gtk-demo, examples/hello-world, examples/browser all set `codegen: false`), where `@gtkx/runtime` hoists to the workspace root and a leftover store under `examples/<x>/node_modules` really would shadow the shared one. The helper never distinguishes that case from the standalone one, so on any project whose store legitimately lives at its own root it deletes the very store the option promises to reuse. The `--force` no-op follows from the same early return: `runCodegen` returns `disabledCodegenResult` at line 133 before `prepareCodegen` and `clearGeneratedStores` are ever reached, so the flag documented in packages/cli/src/commands/codegen.ts:16 as "Wipe the generated store and regenerate unconditionally (recover a corrupted store)" cannot rebuild anything. The misleading follow-on message comes from `undeclaredLibraryError`, which blames the `libraries` list for a namespace that is already in it.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Make the removal conditional on there actually being a shadow. Before deleting anything, resolve where the store belongs — `resolveStore(root)` from @gtkx/codegen already returns `gi.storeDir` and `jsx.storeDir` anchored at the `node_modules` its versioning package resolved from — and compare that anchor with `resolve(root, "node_modules")`. When they are the same directory, the store under the project root is the installed store the option promises to reuse, so `removeSharedStoreShadow` must do nothing; only when the resolved anchor sits in an ancestor `node_modules` (the hoisted/monorepo case the helper was written for, as in examples/gtk-demo) is a project-local `.gtkx/{gi,jsx}` or `@gtkx/{gi,jsx}` genuinely a shadow that would win resolution over the shared store, and only then should it be removed. Resolution can throw when `@gtkx/runtime` or `@gtkx/native` is unresolvable, so the guard should fail closed and skip the deletion rather than fall back to deleting. Apply the same guard at both call sites (`runCodegen` line 131 and `ensureGenerated` line 216) by moving it inside the helper. Alongside that, `gtkx codegen --force` should stop pretending to be a recovery path under `codegen: false`: either keep it a no-op but say so explicitly, or drop the early return so `--force` reports that generation is disabled and the store cannot be rebuilt from this project. Cover it with a unit test that lays down a store under a standalone project root, runs `runCodegen`/`ensureGenerated` with `codegen: false`, and asserts every path survives, plus the mirror test with the store planted in an ancestor `node_modules` asserting the local shadow is removed. Finally, have `undeclaredLibraryError` check whether the namespace is already in `libraries` before telling the user to add it, and report the missing store instead.

rejected.title: gtkx build always writes an ESM bundle to dist/bundle.js, so in a project that declares "type": "commonjs" it reports "Build complete" and emits an artifact node refuses to run
rejected.why: Not a GTK4/GLib limitation, not a documented misuse, not a machine artifact, not a missing feature, and not a duplicate of any of the 48 entries in .bughunt/findings.jsonl (nearest neighbours F101 and R101 are unrelated). It is GTKX overriding correct upstream behavior. Vite 8.2.1 already derives the SSR entry extension from the nearest package.json `type`: chunks/node.js:33649 computes `jsExt = ssr ... ? resolveOutputJsExtension(format, findNearestPackageData(root).data.type) : "js"`, `resolveOutputJsExtension` at :33774 returns "js" only when `type === "module"` and "mjs" for an `es` format otherwise (undefined defaults to "commonjs"), and :33657 sets `entryFileNames: ssr ? `[name].${jsExt}`` with :33658 doing the same for `chunkFileNames`. Verified independently by running plain Vite 8.2.1 SSR builds in a clean temp dir outside the worktree: type=commonjs -> entry.mjs, type=module -> entry.js, no type field -> entry.mjs. GTKX's builder.ts:38 replaces that with the constant "bundle.js", and because `forced` is merged last (`mergeConfig(mergeConfig(buildDefaults, viteConfig), forced)`) it also wins over any user vite.config.ts. The emitted bundle is unconditionally ESM by construction, not by rollup default alone: vite-plugins/settings.ts prepends SCHEMA_ENV_BANNER, which reads `new URL(".", import.meta.url)`, and vite-plugins/native.ts `rewriteLoader` emits `import { createRequire } from "node:module"` plus `import.meta.url`. So GTKX writes an ESM file under an extension whose meaning is decided by the package's `type`, prints "Build complete: dist/bundle.js", and exits 0. Only `entryFileNames` is overridden, so `chunkFileNames` still resolves to `.mjs` in a non-module package, i.e. the override even makes GTKX's own output internally inconsistent. The `"type": "module"` scaffold does not excuse it: Vite would emit `bundle.mjs` for a package with no `type` field as well, and that case only runs today because Node 24's module syntax detection retries the failed CJS parse, not because the name is right.
